issue.title: Bug: [SmartSwitch] DPU gNMI/gNOI service binds to loopback only after sonic-gnmi#712, breaking NPU proxy connectivity

failure.body:
## Is it platform specific

generic

## Importance or Severity

Critical

## Description of the bug

After [sonic-gnmi#712](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-gnmi/pull/712) was merged, the gNMI/gNOI telemetry service on each DPU in a SmartSwitch now binds exclusively to `<IP>:50052` (loopback), making every DPU unreachable from the NPU's internal gNOI proxy.

**Root cause:** In `gnmi-native.sh`, when no `CERTS` or `X509` entry exists in ConfigDB (which is the DPU's default state), the script falls into the `else` branch and hardcodes:

```bash
TELEMETRY_ARGS+=" --noTLS --bind_address <IP>"
```

PR #712 added a strict enforcement in `telemetry.go` (`setupFlags`): when `--noTLS` is set, `--bind_address` must be a loopback address (`net.IP.IsLoopback()`). Since `gnmi-native.sh` already supplies `<IP>`, the service starts — but listens only on loopback.

The NPU's `DPUProxy` (`pkg/interceptors/dpuproxy/proxy.go`) dials each DPU directly at `169.254.200.x:{50052,8080}` over the SmartSwitch midplane fabric using insecure gRPC. With the DPU now bound to `<IP>` only, all those dials fail with `connection refused`.

Note: setting `bind_address` in the DPU's `GNMI|gnmi` ConfigDB entry would not help — the script never reads it, and even if it were passed to the binary, `169.254.x.x` would fail the `IsLoopback()` check and prevent the service from starting entirely.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy a SmartSwitch platform running a SONiC image built after sonic-gnmi#712, with no TLS certs configured on the DPUs.
2. From the NPU, verify DPU gNOI connectivity:

```bash
gnoi_client -target <IP>:50052 -module System -rpc Time
```

3. Repeat for `<IP>`, `<IP>`, `<IP>`. All fail with `connection refused`.
4. On any DPU, confirm the service is listening only on loopback:

```bash
ss -tlnp | grep 50052
# LISTEN  0  128  <IP>:50052  <IP>:*
```

## Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual:** The DPU telemetry service starts with `--noTLS --bind_address <IP>`, binding only to loopback. The NPU's `DPUProxy` cannot reach `169.254.200.x:50052` or `169.254.200.x:8080`, causing all DPU gNOI operations (reboot, time, file) to fail. 100% reproduction rate.

**Expected:** The DPU gNMI/gNOI service should be reachable from the NPU over the `169.254.200.x` midplane fabric. This network is internal and isolated — not exposed externally.

## Relevant log output

```
ERROR:
  Code: Internal
  Message: failed to connect to DPU2: failed to connect to DPU2 on any port [50052 8080]:
  last error: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error:
  desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp <IP>:8080: connect: connection refused"
```

On the DPU (`ss -tlnp | grep 50052`):
```
LISTEN  0  128  <IP>:50052  <IP>:*  users:(("telemetry",pid=...,fd=...))
```

## Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```
SONiC.master-<commit>
```

## Attach files (if any)

N/A

resolution.title: [gNMI] Encrypt certificate-free DPU fallback
resolution.description:
## Why

SmartSwitch DPUs need TLS-encrypted native gNMI on the isolated midplane when no usable server certificate/key pair is configured. Other platforms must retain their existing launch behavior.

Fixes #28540. Source-pointer integration is separate in #28931.

Microsoft ADO (number only): 39179389

## What

- Detect a SmartSwitch DPU when `DEVICE_METADATA|localhost` has `type=SmartSwitchDPU` or `switch_type=dpu`.
- On a DPU only, use ephemeral self-signed TLS when no usable server certificate/key pair is configured.
- Add `--allow_no_client_auth` for that DPU fallback so DPUProxy can connect without a client certificate.
- Preserve configured-certificate, explicit application-authentication, and UDS-only native gNMI behavior.
- Preserve non-DPU transport selection, including the existing plaintext loopback fallback.
- Quote JSON/filter input and normalize top-level JSON `null` to empty so a missing `certs` object does not hide a valid legacy `x509` configuration.

### Examples

| Device metadata | Certificate configuration | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type=SmartSwitchDPU` | none | `--insecure --allow_no_client_auth` |
| `switch_type=dpu` | `server_crt=null`, key configured | ignore the incomplete pair and use the same DPU ephemeral-TLS fallback |
| DPU | complete certificate/key and CA | preserve configured TLS/mTLS arguments |
| non-DPU | none | preserve `--noTLS --bind_address <IP>` |
| non-DPU | `certs=null`, complete legacy `x509` | use the configured `x509` certificate/key instead of treating `"null"` as a `certs` object |

## Validation

- `bash -n dockers/docker-sonic-gnmi/gnmi-native.sh` passed.
- A container matrix passed both DPU metadata forms, no certificates, partial/null certificates, configured certificates, legacy `x509` fallback, explicit password authentication, and UDS-only mode.
- The same matrix compared no-cert, partial-cert, and configured-cert non-DPU arguments with master commit `d7ad3d29d`; all matched.
- On an integrated physical DPU0 image, five of five direct TLS `System.Time` calls and one metadata-routed DPUProxy `System.Time` call passed.

## Scope Boundary

- This PR changes only `dockers/docker-sonic-gnmi/gnmi-native.sh`.
- `docker-sonic-telemetry/telemetry.sh` is unchanged. The DPU TLS fallback is the only intentional transport-mode change; general parsing corrections also prevent top-level JSON `null` from being treated as configured data.
- Source-pointer updates are tracked separately.
- The physical image also contained the source changes referenced by #28931; physical evidence validates the integrated DPU TLS path, not this one-file diff in isolation.
